title: Ram Charan's 'Peddi' Trailer Just Took Over Mumbai — and the North America Pre-Sales Tell You Everything
excerpt: The RRR star's sports drama has already crossed $300K in US pre-sales before its June 4 release. Chiranjeevi called the trailer 'pure firepower.' Here's why the diaspora should be paying attention.
body:
Ram Charan walked onto the stage at Mumbai's Jio World Drive on Sunday afternoon, and for a few minutes, the man who helped RRR become a global phenomenon made everyone in that room forget about everything else happening in Indian cinema.

The trailer for *Peddi* — his most ambitious film since the Oscar-adjacent blockbuster that put Telugu cinema on Hollywood's radar — is now live across five languages, and the early verdict from the industry is unambiguous: this one is different.

## A Sports Drama With Real Stakes

Set in the 1980s, *Peddi* is a sports action drama directed by Buchi Babu Sana, the filmmaker whose debut *Uppena* announced him as one of Telugu cinema's most exciting young voices. The trailer reveals a raw, sweat-drenched world of rural wrestling — think *Dangal* meets *Rangasthalam*, but with AR Rahman's score lending it an operatic scale that neither of those films attempted.

Charan plays a character that producer Naga Vamsi has compared, without apparent irony, to Virat Kohli. "That same intensity, that same refusal to lose," Vamsi told reporters at the Mumbai event. The comparison landed differently for the diaspora fans in the crowd — many of whom flew in specifically for the trailer launch — because they've seen both men perform in person, in stadiums from Hyderabad to New Jersey.

## Chiranjeevi's One-Word Review

The most telling reaction came from Ram Charan's father, Megastar Chiranjeevi, who posted a brief video on social media calling the trailer "pure firepower" and adding, "Well done, Buchi Babu." Coming from a man who has spent five decades in Telugu cinema, that phrasing — specifically the praise directed at the director rather than his own son — tells you something about the kind of film Peddi is trying to be: an ensemble piece where every performance serves the story.

Director Buchi Babu himself has been more specific. In a recent interview, he promised that the film's final 50 minutes would be "heart-touching," a description that suggests Peddi is as much an emotional drama as it is a sports spectacle. The cast reinforces that ambition: Janhvi Kapoor, Shiva Rajkumar (in a role called Gournaidu that already has fans buzzing), Jagapathi Babu as the menacing Appalasoori, Divyenndu in an undisclosed role, and Boman Irani providing what appears to be the film's moral centre.

## The NRI Numbers That Matter

Here's the number that should interest the diaspora: *Peddi* has already crossed $300,000 in North America pre-sales — and the film doesn't release until June 4. For context, that's a figure most mid-budget Bollywood films don't reach in their entire theatrical run in the US.

The pre-sales reflect a Telugu diaspora that has grown increasingly confident about showing up for its biggest stars on opening weekend. Ram Charan's previous film *Game Changer* underperformed domestically, but the overseas numbers were respectable. With *Peddi*, the combination of Mythri Movie Makers' aggressive marketing, T-Series handling Hindi distribution, and a genuinely compelling trailer could push the North America opening past the $5 million mark that separates a hit from a phenomenon in that market.

The film releases globally on June 4, with premieres on June 3 in select markets. It will play in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam — the full pan-India rollout that has become standard for Telugu A-listers but still feels remarkable when you consider that a decade ago, most of these films barely played outside Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

## What's At Stake

The breakeven target for *Peddi* in Telugu-speaking states alone is reportedly ₹220 crore — a figure that would have been unthinkable for a non-franchise film a few years ago. AR Rahman's involvement (his first Telugu film in years) adds both prestige and cost. The film needs to work not just in Hyderabad and Vizag but in Dallas, New Jersey, the Bay Area, and London — the cities where NRI ticket sales can turn a moderate hit into a genuine blockbuster.

For Ram Charan, the stakes are personal too. After *Game Changer* failed to capitalise on the enormous goodwill RRR generated, *Peddi* is less a comeback and more a statement of intent: that he can carry a film that doesn't need a Rajamouli behind the camera to find a global audience.

The trailer suggests he might be right. June 4 will confirm it.

*Peddi releases globally on June 4, 2026. Premieres on June 3 in select international markets. Playing in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam.*
